oneCommandBootstrap.notes: The first candidate exposed empty cloud-image APT indexes; refreshing existing APT package lists fixed dependency resolution. The final public pipe-to-Bash command then installed the signed public package on a new clean guest. Verification checked real API/agent health, root-owned trust, cached package hash, temporary-file cleanup and repeat-install refusal preserving database inode, configuration and service PIDs. This additive bootstrap uses the same production publisher key and unchanged tagged Python installer; existing release packages, manifest and tag were not replaced. ARM64 was exercised for this wrapper; earlier AMD64 package/update/recovery acceptance remains recorded separately.

preexistingBrowserCIFailures.notes: These three browser cases already failed on both CI architectures before the bootstrap change. They remain a separate UI/test investigation; the bootstrap does not change web code, bundles or these tests. This acceptance record does not claim that the full browser suite passed.

codeCI.notes: Formatting, lint, typecheck, unit/integration tests, build and dependency audit passed on the configured CI runners. The browser suite failed the same three cases as the pre-bootstrap commit; full CI is not green. Bootstrap-specific tests and the real public Linux installation passed separately.

old.stderr: bash: line 19: systemd: command not found

ubuntuBootstrapHotfix.notes: The missing-command layout was modeled by temporarily hiding only the systemd compatibility symlink inside a dedicated Ubuntu guest; the running manager binary and services were untouched. The old preflight failed with the reported line-19 error and the fixed preflight passed before any APT action. The symlink was restored before the complete real installation of the signed public ARM64 package. The exact corrected bootstrap bytes were then published and anonymously downloaded with independent signature verification. Only install.sh and its signature were replaced; the original packages, package manifest, standalone Python installer, public key and immutable tag remain unchanged. This does not include the newer source-tree wallpaper in the existing packages. No full browser suite or AMD64 installation rerun is claimed.
